assertions: Validated predecessor and rebuilt successor chains are compared deterministically.
Text, timing, attribution, segmentation, display-label, and source-lineage changes are distinguished.
Only affected predecessor dependencies are invalidated while unaffected evidence remains reusable.
Rebuilt transcript views and context windows are required in the successor chain.
Predecessor machine evidence remains immutable and addressable.
All fifteen required manual review actions are represented in append-only ledgers.
Unknown review targets and review lineage inconsistencies are rejected.
Review queues package source intervals, media access, local context, speaker evidence, proposed actions, and alternatives.
Persistence is reloadable, cache-safe, and tamper-evident.
CLI operations expose propagation impact, manual review, and review queues.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures qualify mechanics rather than correction or reviewer accuracy.
Corpus-scoped successor utterance identifiers change when upstream corpus lineage changes; predecessor mappings preserve addressability.
Temporal utterance mapping is a bounded fallback after canonical word ownership, not semantic equivalence inference.
